title: Projective frames and projective linear transformations over schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $r\geq2$, and let $V$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_S$-module of rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Write $\mathbf P_S(V)$ for the bundle of one-dimensional quotients [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. The automorphism sheaf of $\mathbf P^{r-1}_S$ over $S$ is represented by $G=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,S}$, the open determinant-nonzero subscheme of $\mathbf P_S(\operatorname{Mat}_r)$; multiplication is induced by multiplication of invertible matrices. It is the Zariski sheaf quotient of $\operatorname{GL}_{r,S}$ by scalar units. In particular every projective automorphism is Zariski locally induced by an invertible matrix, and two such matrices induce the same automorphism exactly when they differ by a scalar unit. The functor on $S$-schemes $T$ given by $\operatorname{Isom}_T(\mathbf P_T(V_T),\mathbf P^{r-1}_T)$ is represented by an $S$-scheme, with postcomposition action of $G$; it is Zariski locally isomorphic to $G\times S$ with its simply transitive action. For an invertible module $N$ on $S$, there is a canonical quotient-compatible isomorphism $\mathbf P_S(V\otimes N)\simeq\mathbf P_S(V)$; every isomorphism of projective bundles carries their tautological lines to each other up to tensoring by a line pulled back from the base. All these identifications are natural under arbitrary base change. The group scheme $G$ is smooth over $S$, and any scheme $G$-torsor locally trivial for the fppf topology admits sections over an etale covering of its base.

source.place: Section 4.1.4 (tensoring with an invertible module), Theorem 4.2.3, Remark 4.2.7, printed pp.73--75 (projective-bundle automorphism sheaf modulo scalars). Arbitrary-base formulation via local finite-presentation descent; determinant-open construction also in Milne Algebraic Groups, Example 5.49. Smooth torsor etale local triviality is the usual smooth-local-section criterion, agent expansion. Smooth local sections: literature/stacks-project/more-morphisms.tex, Tag 055U (lemma-etale-nbhd-dominates-smooth).

proof.text: For a line $N$ on $S$, tensor a quotient $h^*V\twoheadrightarrow L$ on an $S$-scheme $T$ by $h^*N$. Tensoring by a line is invertible (its inverse tensors by the dual), so this gives mutually inverse bijections on invertible quotients. The quotient-functor statement of [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] gives $\mathbf P_S(V\otimes N)\simeq\mathbf P_S(V)$. In the direction $t:\mathbf P(V\otimes N)\to\mathbf P(V)$, its tautological formula is $t^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(V)}(1)\simeq\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(V\otimes N)}(1)\otimes p^*N^{-1}$. These bijections commute with every pullback because the quotient and its tensor do.

Let $\alpha:\mathbf P_S(V)\simeq\mathbf P_S(W)$ be an isomorphism over $S$, where both bundles have rank $r\geq2$. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-bundle-picard-classification] to $\alpha^*\mathcal O(1)$ to write it as $\mathcal O(d)\otimes p^*N$. On each residue-field fibre the same classification identifies both Picard groups with $\mathbf Z$ generated by $\mathcal O(1)$; pullback by $\alpha$ and its inverse are inverse group homomorphisms. Hence their integer multipliers have product one, and $d(s)$ is $1$ or $-1$. The pullback of the generating quotient $\mathcal O^{r}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O(1)$ remains generating, after choosing bases of $V_s,W_s$. Negative twists have no global sections by [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology], applied over $\kappa(s)$ with projective dimension $r-1\geq1$; they cannot be generated. Thus $d(s)=1$ for every $s$. The classification now gives globally $\alpha^*\mathcal O_W(1)\simeq\mathcal O_V(1)\otimes p^*N$, proving the asserted tautological-line comparison without a Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Remark 4.2.7: degree one for isomorphisms; arbitrary-base Picard input stated separately

proof.text: Apply step 2 to an automorphism of $\mathbf P^{r-1}_T$. Zariski locally on $T$, trivialize its line $N$, and further restrict to affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The resulting identification $\alpha^*\mathcal O(1)\simeq\mathcal O(1)$ makes pullback of global sections an isomorphism $A^r\simeq A^r$, since [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology] computes $H^0(\mathcal O(1))=A^r$. Its matrix $B$ is therefore invertible. By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], the quotient given by these pulled-back coordinate sections determines $\alpha$ itself. Write $A_0=B^{-1}$ and define $\rho(A_0)$ on quotient points by $q\mapsto qA_0^{-1}$; then $\alpha=\rho(A_0)$. Thus the claimed lift exists locally on the base, including nonreduced affine bases.

source.place: Remark 4.2.7 and Theorem 4.2.3: recover the morphism from degree-one sections

proof.text: Suppose two invertible matrices $A,B$ on a scheme $T$ give the same projective morphism. They provide two quotients from the same free module to $\mathcal O(1)$ on $\mathbf P^{r-1}_T$. By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] these quotients differ by an automorphism of $\mathcal O(1)$, hence by a global unit on $\mathbf P^{r-1}_T$. On every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $T$, [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology] gives $H^0(\mathbf P^{r-1}_R,\mathcal O)=R$, so that unit comes from a unique $u\in R^\times$. Equality on coordinate sections gives $A=uB$, after replacing $u$ by its inverse if necessary. The units agree on overlaps by uniqueness and hence form a unit on $T$. Conversely multiplying a matrix by a unit leaves the quotient class unchanged. This proves the scalar criterion on arbitrary test schemes.

source.place: Theorem 4.2.3 and Remark 4.2.7; scalar kernel via H^0(O)

proof.text: Construct $G$ as the determinant-nonzero open in the projective space with matrix-entry coordinates $a_{ij}$. The standard basis identifies these coordinates with the quotient convention for $\mathbf P_S(\operatorname{Mat}_r)$. By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], a $T$-point consists of a line $L$ and generating entries $a_{ij}\in\Gamma(T,L)$; being in this open says that $\det(a_{ij})$ trivializes $L^{\otimes r}$. On opens where $L$ is trivial the entries form an invertible matrix. Changing that trivialization multiplies the whole matrix by a unit. Conversely local invertible matrices modulo scalar transitions glue to such quotient data. The local maps to $G$ glue uniquely by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Thus $G$ represents the Zariski sheaf quotient of $\operatorname{GL}_r$ by scalar units. Steps 3--4 identify this quotient sheaf with projective automorphisms: local matrices supply surjectivity and the scalar criterion supplies injectivity. Local projective maps and their inverses glue by the same morphism-gluing theorem, so this identifies the entire automorphism sheaf, rather than only its field-valued points.

source.place: 4.2.3 and 4.2.7; agent construction of the determinant-open representing scheme

proof.text: Matrix multiplication and inversion define morphisms on $G$: on local matrix lifts use $AB$ and $A^{-1}$. Their entries are respectively polynomials and the regular functions $\operatorname{adj}(A)_{ij}/\det A$ on the determinant open, so these are morphisms into the invertible matrices. Changing lifts by $u,v$ changes their product by $uv$ and their inverse by $u^{-1}$. The maps therefore agree on overlaps and glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. The formulas $\rho(A)\rho(B)=\rho(AB)$, $I A=A I=A$, $AA^{-1}=A^{-1}A=I$ and $(AB)C=A(BC)$ prove the group identities after the same cover. To check smoothness, work over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ and on $a_{ij}\ne0$, normalizing $a_{ij}=1$. Its determinant-open chart is $R[x_{kl}:(k,l)\ne(i,j),z]/(zD(x)-1)$, with $D$ the normalized determinant. This is standard smooth [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]: choose $z$ as first variable and the one equation $zD-1$; its Jacobian minor is $D$, a unit with inverse $z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth], then [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] over $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The chart is an open subscheme of $G$ mapping into the open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, so clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] makes it smooth over $S$. Source locality now gives that $G\to S$ is smooth.

Choose an open cover $S=\bigcup U_i$ trivializing $V$, and let $\tau_i:\mathbf P(V)|_{U_i}\simeq\mathbf P^{r-1}_{U_i}$ be the resulting projective frames: the open-restriction and free-module clauses of [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] identify $\mathbf P(V)|_{U_i}$ with $\mathbf P_{U_i}(\mathcal O^{\oplus r})=\mathbf P^{r-1}_{U_i}$. On each $U_i$ the desired frame functor is identified with $G_{U_i}$ by $g\mapsto g\tau_i$, using the automorphism representation proved in step 5. On $U_i\cap U_j$, put $h_{ij}=\tau_i\tau_j^{-1}$; the change from coordinates $g_i$ to $g_j$ is $g_j=g_i h_{ij}$. Since $h_{ij}h_{jk}=h_{ik}$ these are isomorphisms of the indicated open subschemes satisfying the gluing cocycle. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] to obtain a scheme $F$ over $S$. Its maps to $S$ glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. For any $T\to S$, sections of $F_T$ correspond to compatible local projective frames. Those projective maps and their inverses glue uniquely by morphism gluing, so $F$ represents the stated Isom functor. On $G\times_SF$, the opens $G\times_SU_i\times_{U_i}F_{U_i}$ cover the source of the action. Their maps $(a,g_i)\mapsto ag_i$ agree on overlaps because $a(g_i h_{ij})=(ag_i)h_{ij}$. Morphism gluing therefore gives the postcomposition action $G\times_SF\to F$; its action identities hold on this same cover and hence globally by uniqueness. Locally this is the simply transitive action on $G$, proving the Zariski torsor assertion.

Every identification above commutes with arbitrary base change. Indeed the generating quotient pulls back to the generating quotient by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]; tensoring by $N$ pulls back to tensoring by its pullback. The matrix formulas, determinant, normalization charts and scalar transitions pull back coefficient by coefficient. Pulling the frames $\tau_i$ back gives an open cover with exactly the pulled-back transition formula $g_j=g_i h_{ij}$, so the represented Isom functor is the base change of $F$. Equality of the locally described maps is global by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing].

source.place: 4.1.3, 4.2.8--4.2.10: pullback of the universal quotient and its morphisms

proof.text: Let $E\to T$ be a scheme torsor for $G_T$ trivialized by a jointly surjective family of flat locally finitely presented maps $T_i\to T$. Fix an affine open $B\subseteq T$. Refine the $T_i\times_TB$ by affine opens. Their images are open in $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], and cover $B$; the affine quasi-compactness argument (a cover by principal opens generates the unit ideal, already generated by finitely many members) gives a finite subfamily. The disjoint union $U$ of these finitely many affine schemes is the spectrum of the finite product of their rings, hence affine, and $U\to B$ is flat and surjective. The inverse image of a principal open under an affine-to-affine map is again a principal open and is quasi-compact by the same argument, so it is an fpqc morphism. Over $U$ the torsor is $G_U$, whose smoothness follows from the same determinant charts in step 6. Thus [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent], applied to $E_B\to B$ and $U\to B$, proves that $E_B\to B$ is smooth. Since $E_B$ is the open preimage of $B$ in $E$, clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] makes $E_B\to T$ smooth. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] to the open cover by the $E_B$ proves that $E\to T$ is smooth. It is surjective: after the covering its fibres are nonempty groups (with their identity sections), and a point upstairs maps to a point of the original fibre.

source.place: Tag 02VL (lemma-descending-property-smooth): finite affine fpqc refinement of a trivializing fppf family

proof.text: Apply [sbc-lem-slicing] to the smooth surjection $E\to T$ from step 9: there is a jointly surjective family of etale maps $U_i\to E$ such that each $U_i\to T$ factors as $U_i\to V_i\to T$ with $V_i\to T$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $U_i\to V_i$ admitting a section $\sigma_i$. Put $v_i:V_i\to U_i\to E$, the composite of $\sigma_i$ with $U_i\to E$. Then $V_i\to U_i\to V_i\to T$ is $V_i\to T$, so $v_i$ is a $T$-morphism, that is a section of $E\times_TV_i\to V_i$. For $t\in T$ choose $e\in E$ over $t$ (surjectivity, step 9) and $u\in U_i$ over $e$; the image of $u$ in $V_i$ lies over $t$. Hence the $V_i\to T$ form a jointly surjective etale cover over which $E$ has sections.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q55-d4e51ddfa (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Fourth delivery of this split. The FIXes on 2d30bd29a938, 12a5e979dde6 and 739095bbab7d were all lost because their landings were refused by the side-completion promotion block. Compared with 739095, both new nodes are byte-identical (cmp). The item differs only in step 6, which adds AA^{-1}=A^{-1}A=I; that is correct and I kept it. The same three faults are back, so I re-applied the repair on this head in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl.json. Sources read: EGA II Remarque 4.2.7 (printed p.75, via pdftotext): Pic P(E) = Z x Pic Y, m=1 for isomorphisms, automorphisms are GL(E)/O^x; 4.2.8 for pullback. Stacks more-morphisms 055U (line 10846) and 0EY4 (line 10957). The statement is true over any S for r>=2. Edge cases tested: r=1 (rightly excluded), empty, disconnected and nonreduced bases, characteristic dividing r. Step checks: step 2 rules out d=-1 because H^0(O(-1))=0 on P^{r-1} with r-1>=1 (twist-cohomology (i)). Steps 3-4 use H^0(O(1))=A^r and H^0(O)=A. The step-6 chart R[x,z]/(zD-1) is standard smooth with Jacobian D, a unit. The step-7 cocycle holds and the action glues. The step-9 refinement is a finite affine, flat, quasi-compact surjection, as smooth-fpqc-base-descent requires. Faults fixed: (1) C4 in steps 6 and 9: 'open immersion etale [def-weil: lfp+flat+unramified], hence smooth by def-sbc [etale = smooth of relative dimension 0]' mixes two definitions that no cited node equates. Replaced by clause (b) of lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes, which also removes lem-trf-smooth-composition. (2) C1 in step 7: P(V)|U_i = P^{r-1}_{U_i} was uncited; it now cites the open-restriction and free-module clauses of quotient-geometry; stmt_deps gain def-pc-fppf-site. (3) D/C5: the 055U node follows in a few lines from the reviewed sbc-lem-slicing (0EY4). Dropped; step 10 is rewritten on slicing; no other node cites it and there is no cycle. The Picard node is true (EGA 4.2.7 extended to arbitrary bases by 0B8W descent), is not a duplicate (every PGL or Picard node on this base is over a field or on P^1) and is not a restatement of the item; kept. Batch-5: lem-trf-smooth-composition is removed by the FIX and is in any case a generic Mathlib leaf. lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent is a generic fpqc descent Mathlib leaf (Stacks 02VL) whose closure has no trf or pd node. lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry is the generic P(E) construction, already a statement dependency of the item, and its closure reaches only Proj/chart construction lemmas. None of these is a step of the trace formula or of Poincare duality, so all are accepted. Accepted tool_uses: quotient-geometry, twist-cohomology, smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine, sbc-lem-slicing.
